title: Thread-Contention and Cache-Line Thrashing on Shared Global Counters
pattern: Using a single global atomic variable to count extremely high-frequency operations across multiple CPU cores.
why_bad: Atomic operations across cores require cache line synchronization. Frequent writes to a single shared cache line cause continuous cache invalidations (cache thrashing), which severely degrades core execution speed and scalability.
detection: Look for global atomic variables updated synchronously across thread boundaries on high-frequency paths.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Permissible if the counter is updated infrequently (e.g., once per second rather than on every network call).
strength: Strong` — limits multi-core execution scaling to the latency of memory-bus syncs.
source: Richard L. Sites - *Understanding Software Dynamics* (2021), Section 11.3, p. 184.
